name: Davy Jones
sources: Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. New York: Benjamin Blom Inc., 1972. Page 15.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Davy Jones is a figure of Scottish and Welsh folklore. The name appears in the phrase "Davy Jones's Locker," a common name for the ocean and the drowned sailor's resting place. Scholars trace the name to a Celtic god who entered his Otherworld kingdom through water. Most rivers in Celtic lands carried goddesses' names, but a few in Britain, such as the Tavy and the Tay, come from the Celtic root taff, the word for stream. That root may have been Christianized into the name Davy. This explains the first name. The surname Jones remains a puzzle. One theory points to Shoney, a Scottish ocean god who lived in the Otherworld and imprisoned the drowned. Under this reading, Davy Jones descends from a Celtic divinity whose locker was the deep sea. Another theory holds that Davy Jones combines the commonest first and last names of Wales, where David appears as Davydd. In that reading the god of the deep is only a sailor's image for the ocean, popularized by Welsh mariners.
objective: The origin of Davy Jones and his Locker, and the Celtic and Welsh roots behind the name.
